fatal_errors: The alloy is incorrectly treated as an initially single-phase solid solution rather than as-cast dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 domains.
The governing intervention—intermediate-temperature aging, particularly at approximately 600°C and 750°C—is omitted and replaced by generic mechanical loading.
The proposed breakdown of short-range order conflicts with the target mechanism of enhanced L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy, restricted cross-slip, and planar slip.
The hypothesis omits jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries and stress concentration at their tips, which are essential to crack initiation and plastic instability.
It predicts a vague monotonic deterioration with temperature or loading intensity instead of the observed non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile transition.
No explicit 550–750°C brittle window or recovery above approximately 750°C is defined.
The proposed falsification experiment does not compare controlled aging states or localize dislocation pile-ups and crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips.
Much of the cited evidence concerns different alloys, ceramics, corrosion, or generic deformation behavior and does not support the claimed embrittlement mechanism.
explanation: The response addresses HEA toughness only at a generic level and does not reconstruct the alloy, thermal-aging intervention, phase-boundary mediator, temperature window, or non-monotonic response. Its central mechanism is also directionally inconsistent with the target: cited evidence E2 associates destruction of short-range order with rejuvenation and softer zones that can enhance ductility, not with the asserted toughness loss. Although in situ TEM or diffraction could be useful, the proposed design lacks an as-cast versus 600°C-aged versus 750°C-aged comparison and does not test whether cracks initiate at jagged FCC/B2 boundary tips without impurity segregation. The falsification rule is broad and partly circular, so it would not distinguish the proposed mechanism from competing causes of fracture.
